_notes: PROSE THE GAME SAYS OUTSIDE A SCRIPTED SCENE (owner rule 2026-08-05:
story elements must not be embedded in code). Everything here used to be
a string literal in a .gd file, which meant a writer could not change a
word without editing a program, and no content tool could see it.
Keys are dotted paths. Values are a string or an array of lines. %s and
%d placeholders are filled positionally by Strings.line/lines -- keep the
order and the count when rewriting, tests/unit/test_strings.gd checks
that every key the code asks for exists and takes the arguments given.
Scene prose does NOT live here -- that is story/prologue/ and the
quests' own steps. This file is the game's own voice: the prowl's
book-keeping, the chronicle's event lines, and the room's captions.

_notes: THE CASEBOOK'S RECORD OF WHAT THE PLAYER HAS DONE.
core/chronicle.gd stores FACTS -- a kind, the ids involved, the numbers
involved. These are the sentences those facts are rendered into, at the
moment the Casebook is opened rather than at the moment the thing
happened. Rewrite a line here and every past entry re-reads with the new
wording; there is no migration, because no sentence was ever stored.
Three of these used to be string literals inside game.gd (law 20).
Keys MUST match Chronicle.KINDS exactly -- tests/unit/test_chronicle.gd
fails on a kind with no template and on a template with no kind. The %s
and %d placeholders are filled positionally in the order that file
declares: ids first, then texts, then numbers.
chronicle_log.prologue_done: The night the kettle screamed. She is gone, and the thread leads into the city. I am writing this down so that somebody has.
chronicle_log.evidence_found: I brought home %s. It means something. I intend to find out what.
chronicle_log.life_spent: I gave a life to %s. The Court wrote it down. So do I.
chronicle_log.court_refused: %s put me down and the Court sent me back stamped REFUSED. I am choosing to take it as a compliment.
chronicle_log.choice_made: I chose %s. I would choose it again, probably.
chronicle_log.quest_done_quiet: Finished %s. Nobody paid me. Some work keeps its own ledger.
chronicle_log.quest_withdrawn: I walked away from %s. It will keep. Work always keeps.
chronicle_log.skill_gained: I know %s now. My body learned it before I did.
chronicle_log.favor_tied: Tied a knot in the thread: %s owes me, and everyone can see it.

_approach_notes: An approach's PRICE is a rule and lives in data/rules.json; its NAME
and what it reads like are writing and live here (law 20). The names
were a `name` field inside CombatState.APPROACHES until 2026-08-05,
which meant renaming 'Case It' meant editing a rules engine.

approach.stalk: Begin hidden. Its first move misses. First hit +1.
approach.ambush: Strike first for 3. It comes up angry.
approach.case: Study it, draw 2 — it studies you back: +1 first hit.
approach.ward: Block 4 that holds through its first turn.
approach.walk_in_desc: Spend nothing. A door is a door.
approach.spool_note: An entrance is paid off the spool. The hand stays yours.

patter.rare: 'Ah. The good shelf. For a discerning paw.'

patter.no_more_tonic: 'You are one cat. There are limits. That was the last one.'
patter.tonic: 'Drink it all. Yes, it tastes like pond. Medicinal pond.'

_notes: THE FIVE MISSION MODULES (docs/design/minigames.md). Every word a
board says: button faces, the running status line, and what an aid
tells you when you spend a paw on it. The boards draw their own
rules-bearing geometry, so this file is the whole of their writing.
Owner pass 2026-08-09: the buttons under a board were the same colour
and the same size as each other, the status line was too small to
read, and three modules explained nothing at all. The teaching lives
in data/minigame_tutorials.json; the labels live here.
Owner pass 2026-08-13: the verbs under a board got bigger again; the
seam says what is wrong with a board that answers every number and
still is not one loop; and the crossing stopped posting a bare humour
at the player. 'What does it mean for the gust to control a specific
energy' was the right question, so the plate now names the thing in
the road and prices it -- a dog you have to hide from, a crowd you
have to weave through, a wall you have to go at.

spool.blurb: What is still wound on, and what is already in the paw. Spent stays spent.
spool.total: %d still on the spool, %d in the paw.

stitch.mirror_banner: MIRROR CHART · the numbers are pinned on backward. The clue on the far LEFT counts the square on the far RIGHT.
stitch.squint_wrong: Squint: the crossed stitch is not in this seam. Take it out.
stitch.squint_sew: Squint: the seam runs along the blue gap. Sew it.
stitch.squint_both: Squint: take out the crossed stitch, then sew the blue gap.
stitch.squint_clean: Squint: nothing is wrong and nothing is missing.
stitch.squint_none: No squints left. The rest of it is yours.

open_seam.loose_end: Every number has what it asked for — but the thread stops in mid-air. A seam is one closed loop: no ends. Find the stitch with nothing carrying on from it.
open_seam.branch: Every number has what it asked for — but the thread forks. Three stitches meet at one hole, and thread cannot go three ways. A seam passes through a hole, it does not gather at one.
open_seam.two_rings: Every number has what it asked for — but this is two rings of thread, not one seam. They have to be joined, which means unpicking some of what is already right.
